pages: I will write it plainly because no one else will. Once in a long while the night goes quiet - no crickets, no wind, no dogs - and on that night you stay inside, and you keep the door shut, and you do not look out of the window when the knocking starts, and you do not answer when it says your name in a voice you know.

It will walk around the house all night. It will breathe against the glass. At some point the Tanner's music box will play, though the Tanner has been dead six years. Stay inside. In the morning count the village. Whoever was out is not lost. Just not here.
